title: Signatures of semantic search in the activations of large language models
abstract: arXiv:2609.35599v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: When recalling lists of concepts (e.g., animals) during the semantic fluency task (SFT), both humans and large language models (LLMs) organise their output into clusters of related items (e.g., sea animals) that are punctuated by strategic switches between clusters. In humans, this pattern can be explained by a semantic foraging process, whereby distinct neural and behavioural signatures accompany within-cluster production ("exploit") and between-cluster switching ("explore"). Whether LLMs likewise represent these two search regimes within their internal states is unknown. Here, we apply a range of mechanistic interpretability techniques to provide evidence for this. In Study 1, we use the Jacobian lens (J-lens), which maps intermediate-layer residual-stream representations to token-level activations, to show that concept-level activations predict switching. First, we find that switching coincides with low next-token activations. Mor

translated_title: 大语言模型激活中的语义搜索特征
translated_abstract: 在语义流畅性任务中回忆概念列表（例如动物）时，人类和大语言模型（LLMs）都会将其输出组织成相关项目的聚类（例如海洋动物），并在聚类之间进行策略性切换。在人类中，这种模式可以用语义觅食过程来解释，其中聚类内产出（“利用”）和聚类间切换（“探索”）伴随着截然不同的神经和行为特征。LLMs是否同样在其内部状态中表征了这两种搜索模式，目前尚不清楚。在此，我们应用一系列机制可解释性技术为此提供了证据。在研究1中，我们使用Jacobian透镜——该方法将中间层的残差流表征映射到词元级别的激活——来表明概念级别的激活能够预测切换行为。首先，我们发现切换的发生与较低的下一词元激活同时出现……
tldr: 该研究通过Jacobian透镜等机制可解释性技术，首次在大语言模型的内部激活中发现并区分了类似人类语义觅食行为的“利用”与“探索”两种搜索状态的特征。
en_tdlr: Using mechanistic interpretability techniques such as the Jacobian lens, this study reveals distinguishable signatures of "exploit" and "explore" search regimes within large language model activations, mirroring human semantic foraging behavior.
